metaHome.title: LUMINA — A self-analysis platform of many lenses
metaHome.description: Psychological assessment (Big Five, emotional intelligence, attachment), a cognitive ability test, and Saju, astrology, tarot and numerology in one place. Every analysis carries the tier and validation status its evidence actually supports.
metaHome.ogDescription: From psychological assessment to cognitive ability and traditional interpretation — a self-analysis platform that says how much each lens can claim. No sign-up.

common.disclaimerCultural: This interpretation is self-reflection content based on traditional symbolic systems, not a scientifically verified prediction. The calculations themselves follow fixed rules — solar terms, planetary positions, shuffle algorithms, and other method-specific logic — but the claim that the results predict life events has not been empirically confirmed.
common.disclaimerEntertainment: This content is entertainment drawn from a fixed bank of phrases, varied by date and zodiac sign or animal. It isn't based on actual planetary positions or personal data, and it isn't a prediction.
common.disclaimerScientific: This result is a self-understanding aid based on a specific scale and reference sample. Sampling, translation, and measurement error limit its scope; it is not a medical diagnosis, clinical assessment, or prediction of future events.
common.nextLensIntro: One result only ever shows one face. Anything you haven't opened yet comes first — one path goes a layer deeper in the same family, the other crosses over to a different kind of knowing.
common.nextLensSibling: Go one layer deeper in the same family.
common.nextLensCrossing: Cross over to a different kind of knowing and compare.

statisticalReading.title: How to read the statistical graphic
statisticalReading.intro: Read the result as a position in a measure and a level of measurement precision, not as a rank, destiny, or verdict.
statisticalReading.observedBody: The dot is the value calculated from this response pattern. It shows a position within the same scale and does not make raw scores from different tests directly comparable.
statisticalReading.intervalBody: The line is a 95% reference interval estimated from reliability. It does not mean the true trait must fall inside it; it makes measurement noise visible.
statisticalReading.referenceBody: The pale band appears only when norms are available. It shows the sample mean and standard deviation, not a Korean norm or a diagnostic threshold.

errors.errorBody: Reload the page or return to the home screen.
errors.notFoundBody: Check the address or return to the home screen.

home.momentLabel: The Saju of this exact moment
home.platformEyebrow: LUMINA / SELF-INQUIRY IN THE AI AGE
home.platformBody: In an age when AI can produce answers in an instant, LUMINA refuses to compress a person into one conclusion. Psychological assessment, cognitive exploration, and East–West interpretive traditions sit side by side as different lenses; each result shows what its evidence can support and where it must stop. No sign-up, and whatever you enter stays only in this browser.
home.heroBody: Solar terms are calculated directly from the sun's ecliptic longitude, not from a lookup table. True solar time is corrected using birthplace longitude and the equation of time, and historical standard-time changes — like Korea's UTC+8:30 in 1954 or daylight saving in 1988 — are factored in as they occurred. There's no sign-up, and anything you enter stays only in this browser.
home.hubHeading: Which part of yourself would you like to meet today?
home.hubIntro: The lenses are sorted by the kind of knowing they offer instead of being mixed into one pile — validated instruments first, traditional interpretation after. Every card carries its tier and validation status.
home.hubSajuDesc: Calculate your birth chart, elements, and life cycles from your exact birth date and time.
home.hubAstroDesc: Explore calculated planetary positions alongside symbolic interpretation.
home.hubTarotDesc: Choose a spread and draw cards for this moment.
home.hubNumerologyDesc: Read tendencies in the numbers of your birth date.
home.hubPsychometricsDesc: Answer 50 questions to see five personality traits.
home.hubJungianDesc: Interpret IPIP-50 responses through four MBTI preference axes while showing continuous scores and boundary uncertainty.
home.hubDarkTriadDesc: Explore three SD3 construct dimensions with a Korean validation limitation notice.
home.hubAttachmentDesc: Analyze patterns in intimate relationships along anxiety and avoidance dimensions.
home.hubEqDesc: Look at self-reported tendencies for noticing and handling emotions with the 33-item SSEIT.
home.hubCognitiveDesc: Work through four ways of reasoning across 16 items in the ICAR formats. No IQ score is produced.
home.hubHoroscopeDesc: Check today's tone by zodiac sign or animal.
home.hubCompatibilityDesc: Compare traditional Saju relationship signals side by side.
home.groupAssessmentDesc: Answer published self-report scales and read where you stand as a continuous score. Each card also names the population the instrument was validated in — and where the Korean translation has not been.
home.groupAbilityDesc: Not self-report: you solve items that have right answers. Because no norm sample has ever answered these items, the result reports accuracy by domain and never an IQ score or a percentile.
home.groupTraditionDesc: Saju, astrology and compatibility calculate a birth moment; tarot and numerology read symbols. Long-standing interpretive systems, used as a language for reflection rather than as prediction.
home.groupTodayDesc: A light read on the mood of the day. It does not predict the probability of anything happening to you.
home.mandalaHeading: Paths into your inner world move around the present moment.
home.mandalaBody: At the center is the Saju of now. The surrounding nodes are the ways you can begin exploring yourself today. Grounded in the actual sky, this map lets different methods lead back to the same inner landscape.
home.mandalaStageLabel: A mandala of today's sky and self-exploration
home.mandalaLegend: Initial node positions use geocentric ecliptic longitude of date; motion follows each body's daily movement. R means retrograde.
home.hubFormPrompt: Choose the “Saju” card above to open the input form here.
home.atlasHeading: How many lenses have you looked through?
home.atlasBody: LUMINA does not define a person with a single result. An outline only appears after several different lenses, so this atlas keeps a record of how far you have come.
home.atlasComplete: You have looked through every lens once. Measuring again after some time may reveal a different outline.
home.atlasPrivacy: This atlas keeps only which analyses you have opened, in this browser. No scores, responses, or birth details are stored or sent to a server.
home.nowBody: Today's day pillar, true solar time, lunar phase, and Mercury's movement become one compact record. The source of each calculation stays visible.
home.nowEvidence: Basis: the day pillar comes from solar-term and stem-branch calculation; lunar and planetary data come from astronomical positions.
home.trustHeading: Fun and evidence share the same screen.
home.trustBody: LUMINA never blends every result into one kind of truth. Badges distinguish scientific measurement, cultural symbolism, and entertainment so you can choose how to read each result.
home.trustScientificBody: Results such as Big Five follow public scales and psychometric principles. We show continuous scores and the limits of measurement together.
home.trustCulturalBody: Saju, tarot, and astrology offer long-lived symbolic systems as paths for reflection. Read them as reflection, not prediction.
home.trustEntertainmentBody: Daily horoscope content is designed to be light and enjoyable. Its entertainment purpose stays explicit.
home.reportHeading: Each method leaves a result in its own language.
home.reportIntro: Instead of making every page feel like Saju, this overview shows what each feature calculates and what kind of question it opens.

saju.dayMasterNote: The Day Master is {hanja} {ko} ({element}). Every other character is read against this one — Ten Gods and Growth Stages both come from here.
saju.pillarFootnote: The bottom row lists, top to bottom: Hidden Stems (Residual · Middle · Principal), Growth Stage, and Zodiac Animal. Void is {void}. The depth each pillar stands at reflects how much weight it carries in interpretation.
saju.tenGodsAside: Relative to the Day Master · eight characters
saju.placeCorrectionEarlier: Corrected to a true solar time about {minutes} minutes earlier than standard time, based on {place}.
saju.placeCorrectionLater: Corrected to a true solar time about {minutes} minutes later than standard time, based on {place}.
saju.calcNote: The Year and Month Pillars are set by solar terms, the Day Pillar by the Julian day number, and the Hour Pillar by true solar time. The lunar calendar isn't used in the calculation — it's shown only for reference.
saju.seasonalHint: Whether the Month Branch supports the Day Master
saju.rootHint: Whether the Day Branch supports the Day Master
saju.peerHint: Whether the remaining characters support the Day Master
saju.strengthNoteStrong: Energy that supports the Day Master dominates. Drawing it down looks closer to balance.
saju.strengthNoteBalanced: Supporting and draining energy are close to even. This doesn't lean firmly either way.
saju.strengthNoteWeak: Energy that drains the Day Master dominates. Adding to it looks closer to balance.
saju.strengthFootnote: Schools of thought differ on how to judge this, so here it rests only on the weighted Five Elements ratio and Seasonal/Root/Broad Support.
saju.tenGodsFootnote: The five groups are split by their Five Elements relationship to the Day Master — which is why their colors match the Five Elements distribution. Branch Ten Gods are judged by the Hidden Stem's Principal Qi, since Zi, Wu, Si, and Hai have a mismatch between their positional and essential polarity.
saju.luckDirectionNote: {direction} · first Major Luck period starts at age {age} ({note})
saju.tenGodGroupSelfGloss: Power like your own — peers and rivals
saju.tenGodGroupOutputGloss: Power you put out — expression and output
saju.tenGodGroupWealthGloss: Power you manage — wealth and results
saju.tenGodGroupOfficerGloss: Power that presses on you — discipline and status
saju.tenGodGroupResourceGloss: Power that helps you — learning and protection
saju.tenGodGuideTitle: A guide to the Ten Gods
saju.tenGodGuideBody: The Ten Gods translate the Five-Element and polarity relationship between the Day Master and another character into traditional role language. These lines do not determine personality or events; they offer a direction for reflection.
saju.tenGodDictionaryTitle: Open the complete Ten Gods dictionary
saju.tenGodDictionaryNote: This is the full dictionary, including relationships that are not shown in the current chart. Ten Gods present in the chart are shown first above.
saju.interpretationLuckNote: Open each period to see its calculated interval and traditional symbolism. These are prompts for reviewing choices and conditions, not predictions of events.
saju.rarityTitle: Distinctiveness of the visible element signature
saju.rarityBody: This is not a population frequency or fortune probability. It counts how often the visible element-count signature appears when 60 sexagenary pillars receive equal symbolic weight.

tenGodReadings.friend: A relationship that shares the same kind of force as the self. Notice the standards you protect when collaborating or competing.
tenGodReadings.robWealth: A relationship in which speed and priorities may differ around shared resources. Reflect on the balance between sharing and boundaries.
tenGodReadings.eatingGod: A relationship that sends thought and energy outward. Notice how you make, express, and care for something steadily.
tenGodReadings.hurtingOfficer: A relationship that looks at existing rules from another angle. Consider the balance between honest expression and relational adjustment.
tenGodReadings.indirectWealth: A relationship with changing resources and opportunities. Set a clear anchor so flexibility does not become scattered effort.
tenGodReadings.directWealth: A relationship with recurring responsibility and practical resources. Check the routines and promises you can sustain over time.
tenGodReadings.sevenKillings: A relationship with pressure and challenge. Consider whether tension can become training and a clearer boundary.
tenGodReadings.directOfficer: A relationship with rules, responsibility, and public standards. Notice where outside expectations meet your own principles.
tenGodReadings.indirectResource: A relationship with learning and recovery outside familiar frames. Notice the time you need to digest things privately and find a new angle.
tenGodReadings.directResource: A relationship with learning, protection, and received support. Reflect on how you accept help and build inner ground.

stageReadings.growth: A cycle in which new energy begins to take root. Notice what you want to cultivate rather than rushing the first step.
stageReadings.bath: A cycle of changing the visible form. Consider whether the way you present yourself still matches what you need.
stageReadings.cap: A cycle of taking on role and responsibility. Think about how you will share what you have prepared with the wider world.
stageReadings.prosperity: A cycle of standing on your own and repeating what works. Notice the difference between self-reliance and rigidity.
stageReadings.peak: A cycle of greater force and visibility. Alongside expansion, consider where restraint and generosity are needed.
stageReadings.decline: A cycle of adjusting a peak approach and handing something forward. Sort what to release from what to keep.
stageReadings.illness: A cycle that invites slower pace, recovery, and care. This traditional label does not mean a health event.
stageReadings.death: A cycle in which one form closes and a transition is prepared. This traditional label does not predict literal death or misfortune.
stageReadings.tomb: A cycle of storing and digesting experience. Notice what needs time to become your own before it is shared.
stageReadings.extinction: A cycle of ending an old connection and setting a new standard. Consider what must be cleared for the next choice to become visible.
stageReadings.gestation: A cycle of holding a possibility that is not visible yet. Care for the conditions rather than forcing an outcome.
stageReadings.nurture: A cycle of protecting and growing a small possibility. Notice the environment and support that make continuity possible.

saju.stageNote: The Twelve Stages are traditional metaphors for the relationship between the Day Master and a branch. Labels such as Illness and Death are not health or lifespan predictions.
saju.luckTransitionNote: Major Luck converts the distance between birth and a solar-term boundary at three days per year, then displays ten-year periods. Boundary readings vary across schools and conversion methods.
saju.yearlyInterpretation: Annual Luck shows the year's stem-branch relationship with the Day Master through the Ten Gods and Twelve Stages. It is a cultural reference, not an event calendar.
saju.noteTimeUnknown: No birth time was entered, so the Hour Pillar wasn't set. The Year, Month, and Day Pillars remain accurate.
saju.noteLateZiHour: This birth falls in the 23:00 hour. The Day Pillar was set using the theory that the day changes at 23:00 — under the midnight theory, the Day Pillar would shift one day earlier.
saju.noteTrueSolarShift: By the clock this falls in the {clockName} Hour ({clockHanja}), but true solar time — corrected for longitude and the equation of time — places it in the {solarName} Hour ({solarHanja}). The Hour Pillar follows the corrected time.
saju.noteNearTermBoundary: This is {hours} hours from the solar term boundary. A slightly different birth time would change the Month Pillar.
saju.noteGenderUnspecified: Gender wasn't entered, so Major Luck was set to run forward. Adding gender determines the actual direction.
saju.noteDST: Daylight saving time was in effect when you were born. The calculation subtracts one hour from the clock time.

saju.dialDaysSince: Born {days} days after the term entry

astro.newTitle: Start a new Birth Chart calculation
astro.newIntro: Enter your birth information to calculate it in this browser, with no sign-up.
astro.heroImageAlt: An illustration of a birth chart and an astronomical observation instrument
astro.balanceNote: This counts which element and modality the 10 planets cluster in. Color isn't used here because astrology's four classical elements are a different system from Saju's Five Elements — using the same colors would make the two look equivalent.
astro.planetsAside: Ecliptic longitude · true equinox of date
astro.aspectsNote: An aspect forms when two planets' angular separation falls within orb of a defined angle. Aspects involving the Sun or Moon use a 2° wider orb — this varies by school of thought, so it's exposed as an option.
astro.calcNote: Planetary positions are geocentric apparent ecliptic longitudes, set to the tropical zodiac with that moment's equinox (true equinox of date) as 0°. Aberration and light-time are accounted for.
astro.wheelCaption1: Ascendant on the left · ecliptic longitude counterclockwise
astro.housePickerNote: The house system changes the spatial partition used to read the same planetary positions. Placidus may fall back to Equal near polar latitudes.
astro.metaDescription: {birthLabel} birth chart — planetary positions calculated astronomically.
astro.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.
astro.wheelAriaLabel: Birth chart wheel. The Ascendant sits on the left and ecliptic longitude increases counterclockwise.
astro.noteTimeUnknown: No birth time was entered, so the Ascendant, Midheaven, and houses weren't set. Earth rotates 1° every 4 minutes, so these can't be determined without a time.
astro.noteMoonSignAmbiguous: The Moon moves about 13° per day. Since the time is unknown, noon was used as the reference point — and this position is close to a sign boundary, so the actual sign could be the neighboring one.
astro.notePolarLatitude: This birth falls within the polar circle. At this latitude there are times when the Ascendant isn't defined, so the value may be unstable.
astro.noteDst: Daylight saving time was in effect when you were born. The calculation subtracts one hour from the clock time.
astro.noteHouseSystem: Houses are calculated with the selected Whole Sign, Equal, or Placidus system.
astro.noteHouseFallback: The birth latitude is near the polar circle, where Placidus is difficult to define reliably, so the chart fell back to Equal houses.
astro.interpretationNote: Planets describe what to notice, while signs describe a traditional symbolic style for expressing it. These combinations do not fix a temperament or predict events; they are prompts for self-observation.
astro.placementFormat: {planet} in {sign} invites reflection on “{theme}” through a {mode} style.

aspectReadings.conjunction: A symbolic conjunction in which two functions gather at one point. Notice how to coordinate them without letting one erase the other.
aspectReadings.sextile: An aspect that suggests room for cooperation. A small experiment can show how the connection works in practice.
aspectReadings.square: An aspect that exposes friction between two functions. Treat it as a place for adjustment rather than a defect.
aspectReadings.trine: An aspect that can feel like an easy flow between two functions. Use the familiarity consciously instead of letting it become automatic.
aspectReadings.opposition: An aspect in which two functions face each other. Try naming both needs instead of removing one side.

psychometrics.metaDescription: A Big Five five-factor personality test built from the public-domain IPIP-50 items.
psychometrics.resultMetaDescription: Your IPIP-50 Big Five five-factor personality test result.
psychometrics.heroBody: These questions are the public-domain items released by the International Personality Item Pool. Responses aren't stored on a server — they live only in the result address — and it takes about 5–7 minutes.
psychometrics.scaleNote: The dot is the raw-score position on this scale (0–100); the band is the 95% reference interval based on measurement error. The percentile and T-score compare this response pattern with an English-language public reference sample — not a Korean norm or a diagnosis.
psychometrics.reliabilityNote: Reliability alpha is the factor-level internal-consistency value published in the official IPIP table. SEM expresses that error in raw-score units. Neither reliability nor the reference interval is a diagnosis or a forecast.

jungian.metaDescription: Interpret IPIP-50 Big Five responses through four MBTI preference axes while showing continuous scores, boundary uncertainty, and a 16-type summary code.
jungian.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.
jungian.kicker: MBTI TYPE ANALYSIS · IPIP-50 REFERENCE INTERPRETATION
jungian.heroTitle: The MBTI pattern in your answers
jungian.heroBody: Answer 50 items to trace four preference axes—E/I, S/N, T/F, and J/P—from your five-factor scores. The result walks you through each letter, continuous score, boundary uncertainty, and type profile, then leaves you with a small experiment question for the present moment.
jungian.whySameItems: How does the MBTI analysis work?
jungian.axesBody: E/I, S/N, T/F, and J/P describe different preferences, not ranks or fixed identities. Start with the continuous score and its 95% reference interval; a near-midpoint axis stays ? so the interpretation does not overclaim.
jungian.methodBody: This screen does not administer new official MBTI items. It linearly maps existing IPIP-50 Big Five factor scores onto four preference axes using correspondence patterns reported in McCrae & Costa (1989). Continuous scores and 95% reference intervals come first; a four-letter code is added only when the axis clears its boundary. Near the midpoint, the letter remains ?.

answer.title: Answer the items
answer.body: Respond to 50 statements from your recent experience. There is no right answer or better type.

map.title: Trace four preferences
map.body: Existing Big Five scores are interpreted across E/I, S/N, T/F, and J/P, with continuous positions and reference intervals kept visible.

reflect.title: Turn the code into an experiment
reflect.body: Use the closest type code as a starting prompt, then test its strengths, cautions, and one small action in your current context.

jungian.sourceMethod: The axis correspondences refer to NEO-PI self-report comparisons reported by McCrae and Costa (1989), not to a user's personal correlation or a new norm. Critiques by Pittenger (1993) and Stein & Swan (2019) are included so the limits of MBTI-style type claims remain visible.
jungian.trademarkNotice: MBTI® is a registered trademark of The Myers & Briggs Foundation. LUMINA is not an official MBTI® assessment, item set, or norm; this unofficial analysis interprets IPIP-50 responses across four preference axes and a 16-code summary using correspondence patterns described in academic literature.
jungian.resultMetaDescription: Continuous scores and a four-letter MBTI-style summary code interpreted from IPIP-50 responses.
jungian.resultHero: {code} compresses the four preference directions that are clearest in this response pattern. The nickname and profile below are prompts for observing your current behavior and choosing a next experiment, not a verdict.
jungian.certaintyLabel: Reference certainty at the closest boundary: {percent}%
jungian.resultReadingTitle: Read the four axes before the four letters
jungian.resultReadingBody: 1) Check each axis score and its 95% reference interval, 2) compare both poles wherever ? appears, then 3) bring the profile's strengths, cautions, and experiment question into your present context. This is a map of today's responses, not a fixed identity.
jungian.axisBoundaryNotice: This axis is close to its midpoint, so no letter was forced. Read both poles—such as E and I—as observation prompts, not a ranking.
jungian.boundaryNote: ? does not mean the result is incomplete. It is a guardrail against using an arbitrary cut point to overstate a continuous response pattern. When a boundary appears, try both preferences in context before deciding what fits.
jungian.typeImageAlt: A self-reflection illustration for the {code} MBTI pattern
jungian.typeImageNote: Use this image as a flexible visual prompt for a pattern that can shift with context, not as a fixed identity.
jungian.boundaryTypeSummary: At least one axis is close to the midpoint, so the full code remains open.
jungian.boundaryTypeDetail: Start with the continuous positions of all four axes. If a result changes, the item responses, present context, or uncertainty near a boundary may have changed; that alone is not evidence that your personality changed.
jungian.openBigFiveResult: Open the original Big Five result

EI.label: Energy preference
EI.description: A continuous direction from recovering inwardly toward gaining energy through people and activity.

SN.label: Information preference
SN.description: A continuous direction from concrete observation toward patterns, possibilities, and new perspectives.

TF.label: Judgment preference
TF.description: A continuous direction from foregrounding criteria and logic toward including people and relationships in the decision.

JP.label: Lifestyle preference
JP.description: A continuous direction from structure and closure toward keeping options open and adjusting to new information.

AT.label: Identity preference
AT.description: A continuous direction from calm self-assurance under stress toward closer, more frequent self-monitoring. This is an original extension not part of official MBTI.

VW.label: Emotional-expression preference

darktriad.metaDescription: Explore Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy construct scores with the 27-item SD3. A Korean validation study did not reproduce the original three-factor structure, so this Korean wording and three-factor scoring remain reference-only.
darktriad.heroTitle: Exploring the darker side of personality
darktriad.heroBody: Uses the 27-item Short Dark Triad by Jones & Paulhus (2014) as an exploratory reference. A Korean validation study reported Machiavellianism and psychopathy loading together in a two-factor solution, so this page does not present its Korean wording or three-factor scores as validated Korean results. Scores are not a clinical or moral judgment.

eq.metaDescription: Explore how you notice, regulate, and use emotions with the 33-item SSEIT. It is a self-report trait scale rather than an ability test, and the Korean translation is not separately validated.
eq.heroBody: Uses the 33 SSEIT items from Schutte et al. (1998) to look at how strongly you report noticing, regulating, and using emotions. The total score is the headline measure; the four subscales are supporting signals that start a conversation.
eq.selfReportNotice: This is not an ability test that measures emotional intelligence through performance. It is a self-report scale in which you describe how you usually see yourself, so a score reflects current self-perception rather than proven skill.
eq.heroImageAlt: An illustration of the four facets of emotional intelligence
eq.visualGuideBody: A score does not define a person. Each image is a metaphor for one tendency, and dedicated illustrations are still in preparation.
eq.resultImageAlt: An illustration representing the four facets of emotional intelligence
eq.totalNormNote: The total-score percentile is estimated by assuming a normal distribution over the Schutte et al. (1998) sample (N = 346, M = 124.78, SD = 13.00). It is not an empirical percentile table.
eq.scaleNote: The total ranges from 33 to 165. Subscales have different item counts, so each is shown as a relative position within its own theoretical range. A high score is not a diagnosis or proof of ability.
eq.reliabilityNote: Published internal-consistency values are reference evidence from prior samples, not a guarantee of reliability for this Korean implementation.
eq.subscaleNormUnavailable: No subscale norms (shown as raw score)
eq.methodBody: All 33 items are scored 1-5, and only items 5, 28, and 33 are reverse-scored. The total is standardized against the published summary statistics in Schutte et al. (1998); subscales follow the four-factor solution of Ciarrochi et al. (2001) but have no published norms, so they appear only as raw scores and relative scale positions.
eq.resultMetaDescription: SSEIT total and four subscale scores, with an explicit self-report limitation notice.
eq.unansweredWarning: {n} items still unanswered. Answer all to see your results.
eq.midpointCaution: Midpoint response rate is {rate}%. Results may be unstable due to many undecided items.
eq.experimentsIntro: These four are not prescriptions but small observation experiments you can run for a week. A lower score is not something to fix; the point is to see for yourself, in daily life, what the items were actually asking about.
eq.experimentsFooterNotice: These are reference results from a self-report scale and do not replace counseling or treatment. If a suggestion does not fit you, it is fine to stop.

perceptionOfEmotion.label: Perception of Emotion
perceptionOfEmotion.blurb: Noticing emotional cues in faces, voices, and your own experience.
perceptionOfEmotion.experimentBody: Once a day, recall a moment that moved you and write down one word for the feeling. After a week, just skim whether the same word repeats or similar situations recur.

managingOwnEmotions.label: Managing Own Emotions
managingOwnEmotions.blurb: Steadying your mood and continuing to try when things get hard.
managingOwnEmotions.experimentTitle: Write down one time it went well
managingOwnEmotions.experimentBody: Pick one moment this week when you got stuck and then started moving again, and write one line about what helped. Next time something similar happens, read that line first.

managingOthersEmotions.label: Managing Others' Emotions
managingOthersEmotions.blurb: Attending to how others feel and to the emotional tone of a relationship.
managingOthersEmotions.experimentBody: Once this week, tell someone close to you specifically what you appreciated. Note how you felt afterwards rather than tracking their reaction.

utilisationOfEmotion.label: Utilisation of Emotion
utilisationOfEmotion.blurb: Using shifts in mood as material for judgment, ideas, and motivation.
utilisationOfEmotion.experimentTitle: Attach one task to your best hour
utilisationOfEmotion.experimentBody: Choose the single hour of the day when you usually feel best, and move one postponed task into it. Check only whether that hour actually helped, not how the task turned out.

cognitive.standardizedBody: This research instrument samples fluid reasoning, verbal knowledge, visual-spatial ability, working memory and processing speed. It uses randomized items and a server-side adaptive design.
cognitive.pilotNotice: This pilot records responses for validation. Right after you finish, you'll see a theoretical-distribution IQ estimate with a 95% confidence interval; once a Korean adult norm is approved, this same screen switches to a standardized score automatically. Subscores and answer keys stay withheld either way.

A theoretical-distribution IQ estimate is shown immediately after completion, and it switches to a standardized score once a Korean adult norm is approved.
cognitive.heroTitle: The way you work a problem
cognitive.heroBody: The pilot samples fluid reasoning, verbal knowledge, visual-spatial ability, working memory and processing speed. Each run draws different items at random while the server adapts selection; finishing shows a theoretical-distribution IQ estimate right away, and this same screen switches to a standardized score once an approved norm exists.
cognitive.heroImageAlt: An illustration of five cognitive domains
cognitive.notAnIqTitle: This is not an IQ test
cognitive.notAnIqBody: Clinical intelligence tests such as the WAIS and the Stanford-Binet are proprietary and are administered one person at a time by a trained examiner. Rebuilding one on a web page is not possible. This page is not a substitute for those tests; it is an exploration in which you work through items in the same formats and look at the grain of your own thinking. Even so, once you finish the items we show a reference IQ estimate right away — always labeled as a theoretical approximation, not a validated test result.
cognitive.noScoreNotice: The result currently shows no IQ score, percentile, standard score or rank. Items must first be calibrated on a Korean adult sample, then pass independent validation, fairness review and norm approval before conversion has a defensible basis.
cognitive.estimateNotice: Finishing shows a theoretical-distribution IQ estimate and its 95% confidence interval right away. Until items are calibrated on a Korean adult sample and pass independent validation, fairness review and norm approval, the screen always labels this as a theoretical approximation rather than a measured norm — and switches to a standardized score automatically once approval is complete.
cognitive.provenanceBody: The items are original LUMINA content informed by the CHC ability taxonomy and ICAR format literature (Condon & Revelle, 2014). We do not copy public research norms; this bank requires its own sample calibration and validation.
cognitive.formatsBody: This gallery previews four public practice formats. The live pilot draws separate items from a protected five-domain CHC bank using randomized and adaptive selection.
cognitive.unaidedNotice: The answer key is downloaded to your browser along with the page — with no backend there is nowhere else to keep it. That is why this result only means something to you if you worked through it unaided.
cognitive.resultMetaDescription: Accuracy in each of the four formats, with the rule behind every item. No norm sample exists, so no percentile and no IQ-equivalent are given.
cognitive.resultSummary: How many items you answered correctly in each of the four formats, together with the rule each item was actually asking about.
cognitive.resultImageAlt: An illustration representing the four reasoning formats
cognitive.domainsIntro: The four accuracies are laid over one shape. A wide or narrow figure is not the size of an ability; it is a picture of which formats sat easily in your hands across these sixteen items.
cognitive.coarseResolutionNote: With only four items per format, accuracy can take just five values: 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100. One item is worth 25 percentage points, so the ordering between formats flips easily by chance alone.
cognitive.reviewIntroResult: This is the part of the page worth staying with. All sixteen items are opened up again, each with the rule it was asking about. Even for the items you answered correctly, reading the rule tends to change how the next one looks.
cognitive.methodBody: The sixteen items are scored only as right or wrong, giving a correct count and accuracy per format and overall. There is no reverse scoring, no weighting, and no time penalty. Time is recorded but is never used in scoring and is never placed in a share link.
cognitive.citationScopeNote: The works below are the source of the item formats this assessment follows, not the source of the items themselves. The norms and validity evidence from that research therefore do not carry over to this result.
cognitive.elapsedResultNote: {minutes} min {seconds} s recorded in this browser — a value that was never used in scoring.

limitations.item1: The items are written by LUMINA in the four ICAR item formats (Condon & Revelle, 2014); they are not ICAR's own items.
limitations.item2: No norm sample has ever answered these items, so no percentile or IQ-equivalent can be given — only per-format and overall accuracy are reported.
limitations.item3: Sixteen items are far too few for a stable ability estimate.
limitations.item4: This is a self-exploration prompt rather than a clinical intelligence test, and the result only means anything if it was taken unaided.

glossaryPage.title: Glossary
glossaryPage.intro: Short explanations for technical terms used in calculated values and interpretations. The evidence tier is kept visible so definitions are not mistaken for validated predictions.

evidenceRef.definition: An internal link from an interpretation sentence to the calculation value it uses. It does not automatically prove the interpretation true, but broken links can be tested.

tenGod.definition: Traditional Saju vocabulary that expresses the Five-Element and polarity relationship between the Day Master and another character through ten roles.

growthStage.definition: Traditional Saju vocabulary that reads the relationship between a Day Master's stem and a branch through a twelve-stage life-cycle metaphor. Illness and Death are not medical or lifespan predictions.

trueSolar.definition: A time value adjusted from standard clock time by birthplace longitude and the equation of time to approximate the Sun's apparent position.

house.definition: A symbolic sector in an astrology chart, dividing the zodiac into twelve areas from the Ascendant and birthplace.

aspect.definition: A calculated relationship that checks whether the ecliptic separation between two bodies is close to a reference angle such as conjunction, square, or trine.

tScore.definition: A standardized score based on a norm sample's mean and standard deviation. LUMINA uses a mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10.

percentile.definition: A 1–99 position showing where a raw response score falls in the reference distribution. It is not a Korean population norm.

sem.definition: An estimate of how much a score may vary across repeated measurement of the same trait, based on reliability and standard deviation.

masterNumber.definition: A numerology rule that keeps 11, 22, and 33 as distinct symbols instead of reducing them to one digit.

jungianAxis.definition: Four continuous preference directions—E/I, S/N, T/F, and J/P—that interpret existing Big Five scores without official MBTI items; boundary uncertainty remains visible as ?.

typeBoundary.definition: A marker used when an axis is close to its midpoint, so an arbitrary letter is not forced. It preserves continuity rather than indicating a missing result.

aboutPage.title: About LUMINA
aboutPage.intro: LUMINA is a self-exploration platform that brings personality, emotion, cognition and cultural symbol systems together in one place. Its guiding rule is to show what a result rests on, on the same screen as the result.
aboutPage.whatBody: There are twelve analyses today. Six sit in the scientific tier, built from openly published scales and literature: a Big Five based trait inventory, Jungian type, the Dark Triad, adult attachment, emotional intelligence, and a cognitive ability exploration. The other six — Saju, astrology, tarot, numerology, daily horoscope and compatibility — are classified as cultural interpretation systems.
aboutPage.tierBody: Every analysis carries an evidence tier badge. Scientific-tier pages name the scales and papers they draw on and state the limits of sample, translation and measurement error alongside the result. Cultural-tier pages say plainly that they are reflective tools built on long-standing symbol systems, not scientifically validated predictions. Never presenting the two as the same kind of claim is a basic rule of this platform.
aboutPage.dataBody: Most analyses store neither your input nor your result on a server. A share link carries the result inside the address itself, so the same link always opens the same result. Where response records are genuinely needed for validation — as in the cognitive pilot — they are stored under an anonymous account, and research use happens only with separate, explicit consent.
aboutPage.limitsBody: LUMINA is not a medical diagnosis or a clinical assessment, and it cannot be used as grounds for hiring, personnel or legal decisions. The IQ figure shown by the cognitive exploration is not a standardized clinical test result either — it is an estimate derived from a theoretical distribution, and the screen always says so.

methodologyPage.title: Public validation methodology
methodologyPage.intro: The fixed test criteria and limitations are shown together so users can inspect the quality evidence behind each calculation engine.
methodologyPage.sajuCases: Saju: all four pillars matched the independent lunar-javascript oracle in 436 cases
methodologyPage.astroCases: Astrology: 200 comparisons across 20 charts plus 803 five-day samples from 2020–2030 × 10 bodies = 8,030 comparisons against astronomia (VSOP87/Meeus lineage), all under 0.05°
methodologyPage.dayCases: Daily pillar: all 73,414 days from 1900-01-01 through 2100-12-31 matched lunar-javascript with zero mismatches
methodologyPage.norms: Big Five: aggregate norms built from 551,607 quality-filtered rows out of 1,015,341 public IPIP records
methodologyPage.determinism: Tarot and numerology: deterministic reproducibility tests for seeded shuffle and digit/letter-value arithmetic
methodologyPage.jungian: MBTI Type Analysis: unit tests fix the linear reference interpretation of existing IPIP-50 scores, four preference axes, boundary behavior, type profiles, and their literature basis
methodologyPage.limitsBody: Saju, astrology, tarot, and numerology use calculated inputs, but their symbolic sentences do not provide empirical validation that future events can be predicted. The Big Five norm is also an English-language online public sample, not a Korean population norm.
methodologyPage.notYet: The 8,030 astrology comparisons use a five-day grid, so they do not guarantee an exhaustive error check for every instant. The Big Five norm is an English-language public sample without age- or gender-stratified norms.

policy.draftNote: Effective 2026-08-18 · This document is a draft and requires legal review before publishing.
policy.privacy1Body: LUMINA works without sign-up or login. We don't collect identifying information like a name, email, or phone number, and no account table exists at all. Inputs like birth date and birthplace are used only for that moment's calculation and are never stored per-person on a server.
policy.privacy2Title: 2. What you enter stays only in this browser
policy.privacy2Body: Your birth info is saved to this browser's localStorage so you don't have to re-enter it. This value is never sent to a server and never leaves this device's browser. You can delete it completely at any time with "Clear My Info" on the input screen.
policy.privacy3Body: When you share a result, your inputs are compressed and embedded directly in the link's address. Anyone who opens that link can recompute the same result (without going through a server). Since no result is stored on a server, deleting the link removes any way to access that result. Identifying information like a name is never included in the link to begin with.
policy.privacy4Body: Your 50 question responses also aren't stored on a server. They're embedded in the result address, and the score is simply calculated on the spot from that.
policy.privacy5Body: If palm-reading analysis is added in the future, our principle is that images are processed on-device only and are never transmitted to or stored on a server.
policy.privacy6Body: Google AdSense ads may be shown to support operating the service. If you decline ad consent, non-personalized ads are shown instead. How Google and other ad partners handle information collected via cookies or device identifiers follows each company's own privacy policy.
policy.privacy7Body: For security and incident response, our web server and hosting infrastructure may retain standard access logs (IP address, request time, request path, etc.) for a limited period. These logs are not linked to any individual profile.
policy.privacy8Body: For questions about this policy, please use the contact details listed within the service.
policy.terms1Body: LUMINA is a self-reflection and entertainment service that combines traditional interpretive systems — Saju, astrology, tarot, numerology — with publicly available academic scales like IPIP-50. Every result screen shows which evidence tier it belongs to (scientifically verified, cultural interpretation, or entertainment).
policy.terms2Title: 2. Not medical, legal, or financial advice
policy.terms2Body: No result may be used as a basis for medical diagnosis, legal counsel, or investment decisions. For decisions involving your health, legal matters, or finances, always consult a qualified professional in that field.
policy.terms3Title: 3. Basis and limits of the calculations
policy.terms3Body: The Saju and astrology calculations (solar terms, planetary positions, true solar time correction, etc.) are based on verifiable astronomical and calendrical data. However, the claim that how these results fall predicts life events has not been scientifically verified. Tarot and numerology follow fixed rules (shuffle algorithms, letter-value arithmetic, etc.) but are likewise not predictive tools.
policy.terms4Body: We maintain a content policy against language that induces fear or states things as deterministic fact. Even so, use under a guardian's guidance is recommended.
policy.terms5Body: Because there are no accounts, we don't apply sanctions (suspension, blocking, etc.) based on user identification. That said, automated bulk requests that threaten service stability may be limited at the infrastructure level.
policy.terms6Body: The service is provided as-is, and we do not guarantee the complete accuracy of calculation results or continuous availability. Our liability for damages arising from use of the service is limited to the extent permitted by law.
policy.terms7Body: When features are added or policies change, this page is updated along with its effective date.

attachment.aboutTitle: What is an attachment style test?
attachment.aboutDescription: Attachment theory describes how relationship experiences can shape patterns in adult intimacy. This exploratory measure is informed by ECR-R concepts and currently reviews its Korean wording, five-point scale, reverse-scoring, and norms. It reports two dimensions: anxiety (worry about abandonment) and avoidance (discomfort with closeness).

attachment.interpretationP1: Attachment style is not a fixed trait but can change with relationship experiences. There is a tendency to move toward secure attachment as you experience safe relationships.
attachment.interpretationP2: Anxious and avoidant patterns are sometimes grouped as 'insecure' in research, but that is not a statement about a person's worth or a pathological diagnosis. Noticing which signals repeat in relationships is a first step toward change.
attachment.interpretationP3: Fearful attachment (disorganized) is a combination of high anxiety and high avoidance. If relationships feel persistently difficult, you can talk with a qualified counseling professional rather than treating a label as a verdict.
attachment.scienceP1: The ECR-R is a widely used reference for adult attachment measurement. This page is not the official instrument: its Korean wording, five-point response scale, and reverse-scoring rules remain under review.
attachment.scienceP2: The four-category model (Bartholomew & Horowitz, 1991) classifies attachment into secure, anxious, avoidant, and fearful based on combinations of anxiety and avoidance.
attachment.scienceP3: No production percentile or Korean population norm is shown. Raw sums and means are presented as exploratory signals only; the retained historical estimates are not used in this result.

states.errorTitle: The vault could not be read
states.errorBody: The saved results could not be checked safely. Please try again in a moment.
states.lockedTitle: A few more lenses are needed
states.lockedBody: The integrated portrait opens after three distinct personal analyses and two distinct scientific provenance groups. The current counts are shown below without adding scores.
states.unlockedBody: Each observation stays within its source tool's scope. Scores are never collapsed into one intelligence or personality total.

hero.title: One scene made from several lenses
hero.line: This current portrait draws from {analyses} analyses and {perspectives} scientific provenance groups.
hero.limit: The character is a memory aid, not a visual translation of high or low scores or a measure of human worth. It is not for diagnosis, prediction, or placement.

composition.title: What makes up this portrait
composition.description: The bars count the analyses, sources, and observations gathered on this page. They do not combine different lenses into one score.

lanes.scientificBody: These signals come from published scales and exploratory self-report tools. Results that re-express the same IPIP-50 responses are not counted as independent evidence.
lanes.culturalBody: Saju, astrology, and numerology stay outside scientific scores and remain prompts for reflection.

claim.singleSource: A single-source observation beginning with the signal “{signal}”. It is not a conclusion made by adding another tool's score.
claim.none: There are no observations to show in this lane yet.
claim.limit: This observation carries the source tool's scoring, sample, and translation limits. Treat it as a prompt to check in daily life, not a verdict about you.

controls.title: Manage your records
controls.body: The latest result for each analysis is used in the portrait by default. You can exclude a result, delete the vault, or export the current derived summaries as JSON.
controls.privacyBody: The browser vault is not encrypted storage that protects against someone who can access this device and browser. Raw responses and birth details are not stored, but on a shared device choose not to save or delete everything after use.
controls.operationError: The request could not be completed. Please try again in a moment.

entry.title: See several results in one scene
entry.body: Bring completed analyses together by evidence lane using safe derived summaries. Raw responses and birth details are not stored on this page.

atlas.body: There are {count} results in the integrated vault.

admin.title: Admin analytics
admin.genericError: Check your sign-in details or confirm that administrator access is configured.
admin.accessNote: A private operations console for LUMINA traffic and solution usage.
admin.setupNote: Administrator authentication is not active yet. Configure authentication and membership in the deployment environment first.
admin.accessDeniedBody: This screen is available only to registered administrator accounts.

adminAnalytics.title: Traffic and solution usage
adminAnalytics.description: Review daily and period traffic alongside solution entry, completion, result, and sharing flows.
adminAnalytics.trafficDescription: Daily pageviews and visitors in Korea Standard Time. Visitors are unique within the selected period.
adminAnalytics.solutionUsageDescription: Compare each solution from solution entry through result view. Test starts remain a separate diagnostic count and do not double-count entries.
adminAnalytics.funnelDescription: Event counts for the selected period. Choose a solution to narrow the funnel.
adminAnalytics.noData: There is no data to display.
adminAnalytics.partialNote: The rollup is older than 48 hours. Treat period comparisons and visitor totals as directional.
adminAnalytics.configureSource: Configure the Vercel Analytics read token to enable live aggregates.
adminAnalytics.migrationRequired: The operations migration and administrator membership must be configured before data can appear.
adminAnalytics.approximateVisitors: Rollup-period visitors are the sum of daily unique visitors and are directional; they may differ from a unique count for the full period.
adminAnalytics.accessDeniedBody: Only registered administrator accounts can view the analytics dashboard.

consent.message: This site may show ads and collect anonymous visit statistics to support its operation. If you consent, ads are based on your interests; if you decline, ads are shown without personalization — visit statistics are collected the same way either way.

share.summaryOnlyNotice: This page shows a summary someone else shared with you. Item-level responses and detailed subscale breakdowns aren't available or appropriate here.
share.ctaTitle: Curious what your own pattern looks like?
share.ctaBody: This summary was generated from someone else's answers. Take the same analysis yourself to see your own continuous scores and boundary axes.
share.invalidBody: The code in this link is missing or damaged. Ask the sender for a fresh link, or take the analysis yourself.

jungian.metaDescription: A summary someone shared from LUMINA's MBTI-style analysis: continuous axis scores mapped to the {code} pattern, derived from Big Five responses.
jungian.heroBody: Someone shared this MBTI-style summary computed from their IPIP-50 Big Five responses. The four letters compress four continuous preference axes — a boundary axis stays "?" instead of forcing a letter.
jungian.footerNotice: Derived from Big Five · not the official MBTI® instrument

fallback.metaDescription: This link carries a summary from LUMINA's {title} analysis.
fallback.heroBody: This link carries a summary from LUMINA's {title} analysis. Open the full analysis to see your own result.
fallback.footerNotice: Summary only · open the full analysis for details

bigfive.footerNotice: Evidence from an English-language reference sample · not Korean-normed

darktriad.footerNotice: Not a clinical diagnosis or moral judgment — Korean research hasn't replicated the original three-factor structure.

attachment.footerNotice: This implementation doesn't match the official ECR-R items, 7-point scale, or reverse-scoring rules — shown as experimental only.

eq.footerNotice: Self-report trait measure, not an ability test · Korean wording is an unvalidated translation

cognitive.footerNotice: 16 items written by LUMINA in ICAR formats · no norm sample, so no percentile and no IQ-equivalent · not a clinical IQ test
cognitive.footerNoticeV2: Theoretical-distribution research estimate · not an approved norm · not a clinical IQ test
